scope_limits: Two-word model: vowel word p = 1-8, consonant word q = 1-16, and 7 checks after the phase penalty are needed, so long pairs are undecided (roughly p + q above 15; a vowel word of 8 or more is free and then the consonant word must be 8 or shorter). Vowels are A E I O U; the clues hold no Y, so Y as a plain vowel is the same test. Class by cipher letter: the K4 clue ciphertext has no A E I O U, so that test is a plain repeating key of 1-16 with a free phase at BERLINCLOCK (plus Y at position 64 as the only vowel). Holding key: L = 2-16 on named sets only (vowels, consonants, letters of KRYPTOS, each single clue letter on the plain or cipher side, a cipher letter equal to the one before); arbitrary sets only as subsets of the 13 clue plaintext letters, only on A-Z, KRYPTOS and 84 theme-word alphabets, L = 2-12; no arbitrary cipher-letter sets. A hold is exactly 0 and a skip exactly 2 places; no restart, no longer jumps, no three classes of letter. Tableaux: A-Z, KRYPTOS, dictionary keyword alphabets and their two transposition-mixed forms, five layouts, Vigenere, Beaufort (variant Beaufort is covered by Vigenere); no hidden alphabet, no transposition layer. The key words themselves may be any letters (not only dictionary words). Controls ran on a third of the alphabets each. Planted answers used class by plain letter only.

negative.family: text-dependent key place: vowel word and consonant word, or a key that holds on a letter set
negative.hypothesis: K4 is a keyword-tableau cipher in which vowels take key letters from one repeating word and consonants from another, each moving on only when used, or one repeating key that holds or moves two at or after the letters of a set.

follow_ups: The two-word cipher is ambiguous for its own reader: with the right key and both clues fixed, 30 planted English messages had 384 to 41 million consistent readings (median about 19,000), because the reader must guess the class of each letter. A cipher meant to be solved is unlikely to work this way unless the class is visible in the ciphertext; a variant where the class is marked by position or by the previous cipher letter is unambiguous and not tested here.

Three classes of letter (for example vowels, the letters of KRYPTOS, the rest), each with its own word: the same equal-pair mask machinery in kryptos/idea111_classes.py does it with one more side table.
